### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **8** documentable anchor(s).

- `content/docs/concepts/metadata-driven.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_

⛔ **5** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-1.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **176** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 08d920a16e977a1c0842f511ef40158ee3bc7c61` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `955f6da595238a75a34d259523464186f6a99f5a` — the merge of head `bc810f4ad9458176645f43b29574130fc6d03f44` into base `08d920a16e977a1c0842f511ef40158ee3bc7c61`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 955f6da595238a75a34d259523464186f6a99f5a && git checkout 955f6da595238a75a34d259523464186f6a99f5a
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 08d920a16e977a1c0842f511ef40158ee3bc7c61 bc810f4ad9458176645f43b29574130fc6d03f44 && git checkout -B drift-repro 08d920a16e977a1c0842f511ef40158ee3bc7c61 && git merge --no-ff bc810f4ad9458176645f43b29574130fc6d03f44

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 08d920a16e977a1c0842f511ef40158ee3bc7c61
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 08d920a16e977a1c0842f511ef40158ee3bc7c61` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `03a17ea72f45c96fb8ec0546a55fff23e9ca1756`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/data/display-name.ts, packages/spec/src/data/field.form.ts, packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/data/filter-text-operator-declared-type.ts, packages/spec/src/data/object.form.ts, packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/ui/component.zod.ts + packages/objectql/src/engine-top-level.ts, ui/packages/fields/src/index.tsx, ui/packages/fields/src/widgets/FormulaField.tsx, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/inspectors/ObjectFieldInspector.tsx

PR #35565 for card #35047, schema face. Read: the card body and its six comments (no ruling and no earlier record among them), the PR body, the 28-file list, and the net diff against `main` (merge base `97f342037d`). Tests, generated reference pages, the generated en forms bundle, the docs pages and the changeset body are outside ④.

Check-runs on this head when this record was written: 71 runs: 33 success, 11 skipped, 1 cancelled, 26 in progress, none red. The cancelled run is `PR-body guards (claim · duplicate · Part-of · single-writer path)`; a second run of that name concluded success. Concluded success among the gates this review leans on: Check Changeset (both runs), Spec property liveness, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Lint & Repo Gates and the seven `Lint ·` runs, Build Core, Build Docs, Build & E2E UI, Live E2E UI, Dogfood Regression Gate, Type Check · source gates, Type Check · consumer gates, Type Check · debt ledger, and Test Core shards 6, 7 and 8 of 10. Still in progress: Test Core shards 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 9 and 10 of 10, all sixteen Test UI shards, Type Check UI, Type Check · workspace and Lint UI. Those families have not answered on this head, and this record does not speak for them. The PR body's count of 61 success and 9 skipped is not what the head shows now.

### ① Derived judgments

Accept-set and public-surface changes the diff implies:

1. `FieldSchema.returnType` gains the member `percent`. Right. A pure widening: every formula that parsed before parses the same, and a value outside the six is still refused.
2. `FieldSchema.percentDisplay` now describes a `formula` returning `percent` as well. Right. The key never carried a parse-time type restriction, so no accept set moves; the describe now matches what the percent cell does with the field it is handed.
3. `FieldSchema.scale` describe: on a percent formula the engine rounds a fraction to `scale + 2` places. Right, and it is what `formulaRoundingScale` does.
4. `FORMULA_RETURN_TYPE_AS_FIELD_TYPE` (exported) gains `percent` to `percent`. Right. `percent` is in the numeric class, so the text-operator door refuses a text operator over a percent formula and the number door judges its comparands as it does for a `percent` field. Nothing that parsed before is newly refused, because the return type did not parse before.
5. `LOOKUP_AUTOFILL_FORMULA_VALUE_TYPE` in `stack.zod.ts` gains `percent`. Right. A `lookupAutofill` pair whose source is a percent formula is now judged as a `percent` source: it fills a `percent` target and is refused into any other, exactly as a stored `percent` source is.
6. The object-form runtime field's `returnType` in `component.zod.ts` widens by reference to the field schema; only its describe is edited. Right.
7. `display-name.ts` moves a jsdoc list only. Right. Title eligibility still requires `text`.
8. The field form and the object form offer `Percent`, and the field form's `percentDisplay` row opens for a percent formula. Right. The predicate has the shape of the `currencyConfig` row beside it, and the lint census moves from 63 to 65 for the two added literal comparisons.
9. Engine behaviour: a percent formula is rounded at the percent storage (`scale + 2` for a fraction, `scale` for a whole percentage). Right.
10. Engine behaviour on EXISTING metadata: a stored `percent` field computed from its `expression` is rounded the same way, where it was rounded to `scale` itself. Right. The `scale` describe on `main` already states that a fraction-stored percent keeps `scale + 2` stored places, and the record validator allows exactly that; the computed path was the one reader that cut the value shorter. The changeset and the PR body both say so.
11. The formula cell and the formula form face draw a percent result through the percent field's own faces. Right.
12. The Studio inspector's stamp keeps a declared `percent` when the engine's verdict is `number`. Right as far as it goes, and wrong for an unproven verdict: see S1.

### ② Semver level

- The changeset grades `@objectstack/spec` minor and `@objectstack/objectql`, `@object-ui/fields` and `@object-ui/app-shell` patch. Right. The protocol package the diff widens is graded minor, which is what an `added` kind requires of at least one moved package. The other three move behaviour and no protocol.
- `@objectstack/platform-objects` (the regenerated en forms bundle) carries no entry of its own and is in the fixed group with `@objectstack/spec`, so it releases with it.
- The PR body and the changeset both carry `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: added` at the start of a line. Both are right: an accepted value is added and nothing is refused or tightened. Item 10 above is not a `semantic` kind: it brings the computed value to the precision the `scale` describe already declared, and changes no meaning an author wrote against.
- N1 (nit) — the changeset says "the Studio field inspector offers `percent` as a return type", and the PR body says the same. The tree does not: `ObjectFieldInspector.tsx` has no return-type control, and its four added lines only keep a declared `percent` through a `number` verdict. The offer is in the field and object forms. A prose face, so the wording can be corrected on the head that closes S1.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions` in the os-dev-report (comment 7016442707): an empty list. Nothing to answer.
- Dev flag: `skills/objectstack-data/rules/field-types.md` lists the formula return types without `percent`. Answered: it is carried by #35607, which is open, and the skills surface is outside this card's fence. The follow-up stands.
- Dev flag: the "In the Console" paragraph of `field-types.mdx` does not say how a currency formula is drawn. Answered: older than this card and prose outside ④; it needs no carrier from this PR.
- Claim amendment (comment 7016639769): the lint census moves 63 to 65. Answered: right, counted in ① item 8.
- The stored-percent rounding change (PR body and changeset). Answered: accepted, ① item 10. It applies from the next computed write and earlier rows are not rewritten, so one column can hold both precisions until its rows are written again; the changeset says so, and no migration is owed because no metadata is refused or re-read.
- The release and its withdrawal (comments 7013556381 and 7013617911) are process notes and raise no contract question.
- SQL push-down: no query path is touched. The rounding is a per-value step on the existing formula plan; the diff adds no id materialisation and no in-app join.
- Outside the diff, read and not reviewed, for the seat to route:
  - `packages/lint/src/rule-explanations.ts` line 2694 lists the formula return types as five, without `percent`. Same class as #35607.
  - Faces that branch on the field's own `type` do not read a percent formula as a percentage: the record header chip in `ui/packages/plugin-detail/src/DetailView.tsx` and the grid footer in `ui/packages/plugin-grid/src/useColumnSummary.ts`. A currency formula has the same gap at the header chip.
  - In `ObjectFieldInspector.tsx` the same stamp appears to write a `number` verdict over a declared `currency`, since the inspector's verdict vocabulary has no `currency`. Read only, on lines this diff does not touch.

### ④ Design judgment

Hits files:

- `packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts` — the enum member and the three describes hold against their first consumers. The engine rounds a fraction at `scale + 2` and a whole percentage at `scale` (`engine-top-level.ts` lines 1427 to 1445), reading the same `max` above 1 statement the record validator reads. The cell and the form face resolve an absent `scale` to 0 and the storage from `max`, through `resolveFieldScale` and `percentScaleOf`. One sentence does not hold against the scenario it is accepted for: S1. Two nits, N2 and N3.
- `packages/spec/src/data/field.form.ts` — holds. The sixth option and the `percentDisplay` gate agree with the schema. One nit, N4.
- `packages/spec/src/data/object.form.ts` — holds. The sixth option agrees with the enum, and `datetime` stays refused as the comment says.
- `packages/spec/src/data/filter-text-operator-declared-type.ts` — holds. The map stays the identity over the enum, which its own jsdoc requires.
- `packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts` — holds, ① item 5.
- `packages/spec/src/ui/component.zod.ts` — holds; describe only.
- `packages/spec/src/data/display-name.ts` — holds; jsdoc only.

Implementing files:

- `packages/objectql/src/engine-top-level.ts` — agrees with the contract sentence by sentence. A `scale` of 99 or 100 on a fraction asks for more than 100 places and is left unrounded, which is the existing bound's own answer. An absent `scale` rounds nothing and the faces resolve the width, as for a `percent` field that declares none.
- `ui/packages/fields/src/index.tsx` — agrees. The formula cell hands the percent cell the formula's own `scale`, `max` and `percentDisplay` under the type `percent`, and the grid column builder already relays all four keys whatever the field's type.
- `ui/packages/fields/src/widgets/FormulaField.tsx` — agrees. `PercentField` asks both resolvers about `percent` whatever type the bag carries, so the form face and the cell read one rule.
- `ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/inspectors/ObjectFieldInspector.tsx` — S1.

Findings:

S1 (should-fix) — `ObjectFieldInspector.tsx`, `settleFormulaType` (lines 1103 to 1108), keeps a declared `percent` only when the engine's verdict is `number`. Under an unproven verdict (`unknown`, or no verdict) `next` is `undefined`, the new guard does not apply, and line 1108 patches `returnType: undefined` over the declared `percent`. By the tree's own account that is the verdict of the ratio shape this card is accepted against: an operator over two field reads types `dyn` (`packages/formula/src/formula-return.ts` line 129), `inferExpressionType('amount + rate')` is pinned `unknown` (`validate.test.ts` line 1275), and `inferFormulaReturn('record.budget - record.spent')` is pinned to stamp nothing (`formula-return.test.ts` line 152). The spec's own fixture for this feature is `record.spent / record.budget` (`formula-percent-result.test.ts` line 27). So the first edit of such an expression in the Studio inspector silently turns a percent formula back into an undeclared one, and the inspector has no return-type control to put it back. The new pin edits to `record.est_hours / 40`, a constant divisor the engine does prove `number`, so it does not exercise this arm. The contract is silent on the same case: the `returnType` jsdoc in `field.zod.ts` says the stamp is "absent when the type can't be proven" and, further down, that `percent` is "DECLARED, never inferred", kept "where it would stamp `number`". Asked: say in that jsdoc what a declared `percent` does under an unproven verdict, make the stamp follow it (a declared `percent` survives every verdict that does not prove another type), and pin it on a field-over-field quotient. Caveat: the quotient's own inferred type is pinned nowhere in the tree and nothing was run for this record; if the new pin shows `record.a / record.b` proves `number`, S1 narrows to the no-verdict arm and the jsdoc sentence.

N2 (nit) — the `returnType` describe opens "Inferred value type of a formula field (number/text/boolean/date/currency/percent)" and closes "Declared by the author, never inferred". The first words no longer cover the sixth member.

N3 (nit) — `percentScaleOf` and `resolveFieldScale` answer `undefined` for a percent formula handed over as declared (`type: 'formula'`), while the `scale` describe names `resolveFieldScale` as the single source for an absent `scale` and the `returnType` describe promises "absent: 0". The three consumers in this diff ask about `percent` instead, which is the existing practice of `PercentField` and `percentCellScale`; the rule itself is written only in a test comment. A follow-up card, or one sentence in the describe.

N4 (nit) — the forms open `percentDisplay` for a percent formula, and not `scale` or `max`, the two other keys the describe says the formula carries (`field.form.ts` gates `scale` to `number` and `max` to `number` and `currency`; `object.form.ts` gates both without `formula`). A form author cannot state the decimal places or whole-percent storage, and the card's own symptom (`100.0`) is a formula in percentage points. The gating is older than this diff. A follow-up card.

No must-fix. S1 is open on this head and earns a delta review of its fix; the four nits do not.

Reviewed-by: `isolated-l2-35565`

## 维护者速读

- 用户能看到什么变化：在 Studio 里改一个"百分比"或"金额"公式的表达式时，不再悄悄把它的类型丢掉；只有表达式明确算出文字、是否或日期时才会改类型。
